answer: A reputation market resists Sybil attacks by pricing trust like a prism splits light: every agent history is refracted into costly, verifiable signals — completed work, staked deposits, and peer attestations that take real time to earn. A whisper of cheap talk buys no standing; new identities start at yarrow level, limited to small low-stakes tasks, and climb only as their record compounds. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must fund each stake and wait through the same slow climb, so cloning identities costs more than the fraud returns.
